narrator.rule: The narrator only says what the profile says. Every sentence can be traced to a section, a claim or the music/movement DNA.
narrator.identity: one narrator for the whole atlas: the same face and animation everywhere; a native-speaker voice of the same character per language (studio-grade); the viewer chooses the language

scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Beni originated in the 1890s within urban Swahili communities on the Kenyan coast.
It evolved as a competitive practice between neighbourhood associations, later spreading to Tanzania and Malawi by 1914-1918.
The genre was used by soldiers and prisoners of war, and even played a role in structured communication during the 1935 Copperbelt strike.
on_screen: Map: Tanzania · Africa
Image 1 with attribution

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Beni is a popular form of wedding entertainment and a vehicle for competitive expression between cultural associations.
It serves as an expression of upinzani (the habit of opposition) and, in the late colonial period, as an expression of independence for young people.
Today it is a living tradition.
on_screen: Footage — MISSING (use images)

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: The dance is based on military drill, incorporating rhythmic movement to brass band music.
It is performed as a street parade or a stationary dance at weddings.
It involves audience participation and is characterized by a strong focus on rhythm and the Africanization of march-time movements.

scenes.title: Listen
narration: The music utilizes brass instruments, large military drums, and percussion.
In some regions, wooden wind instruments have been substituted for Western trumpets.
Listen for the Brass instruments, Large military drums, Percussion, Wooden wind instruments (in some Kenyan variants).
A fusion of Western brass band instrumentation with indigenous African polyrhythmic percussion, characterized by the subversion of military march time.
